verses.text: They brought God's ark in and set it inside the tent David had set up for it. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.
When David had finished offering the burnt offerings and peace offerings, he blessed the people in the LORD's name.
Then he gave every Israelite, man and woman, a loaf of bread, a portion of meat, and a raisin cake.
He appointed some of the Levites to serve in front of the LORD's ark, to call on, thank, and praise the LORD, the God of Israel.
Asaph was the leader, and Zechariah was second. Then came Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, Obed-Edom, and Jeiel, who played harps and lyres. Asaph played loud cymbals.
Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests were to blow trumpets regularly in front of the ark of God's covenant.
That day David first gave Asaph and his relatives the job of giving thanks to the LORD with this song:
Give thanks to the LORD! Call on his name! Tell the nations what he has done.
Sing to him! Sing praises to him! Tell about all his wonderful works.
Be proud of his holy name. Let the hearts of those who look for the LORD be glad.
Look to the LORD and his strength. Always look to him.
Remember the wonderful things he has done, his miracles, and the judgments he has spoken,
you descendants of his servant Israel, you children of Jacob, his chosen ones.
He is the LORD our God. His judgments are seen in all the earth.
Remember his covenant forever, the promise he made for a thousand generations.
It is the covenant he made with Abraham, the promise he swore to Isaac.
He made it a law for Jacob, an everlasting covenant for Israel.
He said, "I will give you the land of Canaan as your share to keep."
This was when you were only a few people, very few, and strangers in the land.
They wandered from nation to nation, from one kingdom to another.
He did not let anyone harm them. He warned kings because of them:
"Do not touch my anointed ones! Do not harm my prophets!"
Sing to the LORD, all the earth! Tell about his salvation every day.
Tell the nations about his glory. Tell all peoples about his wonderful works.
The LORD is great and most worthy of praise. He is to be respected above all gods.
All the gods of the nations are only idols, but the LORD made the heavens.
Honour and majesty surround him. Strength and joy fill his dwelling place.
Give to the LORD, you families of the nations, give to the LORD glory and strength!
Give to the LORD the glory his name deserves. Bring an offering and come before him. Worship the LORD in the beauty of his holiness.
Tremble before him, all the earth. The world stands firm. It cannot be moved.
Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice! Let them say among the nations, "The LORD is King!"
Let the sea and everything in it roar! Let the fields and everything in them be joyful!
Then the trees of the forest will sing for joy before the LORD, because he is coming to judge the earth.
Give thanks to the LORD, because he is good. His faithful love lasts forever.
Say, "Save us, God our Saviour! Gather us and rescue us from the nations, so we can give thanks to your holy name and be glad as we praise you."
Praise the LORD, the God of Israel, forever and ever. Then all the people said, "Amen!" and praised the LORD.
David left Asaph and his relatives there in front of the ark of the LORD's covenant, to serve there regularly, as each day's work required.
He also left Obed-Edom and his sixty-eight relatives to serve with them. Obed-Edom son of Jeduthun and Hosah were gatekeepers.
David left Zadok the priest and his fellow priests in front of the LORD's tabernacle at the high place in Gibeon.
They were to offer burnt offerings to the LORD on the altar of burnt offering regularly, morning and evening, following everything written in the Law of the LORD, which he gave to Israel.
With them were Heman, Jeduthun, and the others chosen by name to give thanks to the LORD, "because his faithful love lasts forever."
Heman and Jeduthun were in charge of the trumpets, the cymbals, and the other instruments for the songs of God. The sons of Jeduthun were stationed at the gate.
Then all the people went home, and David went back home to bless his family.
